content.value_statement: Distributed workflows often fail through unclear boundaries, unsafe retries, or nondeterministic logic. This skill provides Temporal patterns for resilient orchestration and recovery.
actual_capabilities: Distinguishes deterministic workflow logic from external activity work.
Explains saga compensation ordering for distributed transactions.
Guides entity workflows, parallel execution, and asynchronous callbacks.
Identifies nondeterministic operations that break workflow replay.
Recommends retry, timeout, heartbeat, and idempotency practices.
Provides scaling and monitoring considerations for Temporal workers.
limitations: Provides architecture guidance rather than production-ready implementation code.
Does not inspect or test an existing Temporal deployment.
References an implementation playbook that is not included in this package.
Requires environment-specific validation for retry limits, payload sizes, and capacity.

use_cases.title: Design Order Compensation
use_cases.description: Plan inventory, payment, and fulfillment steps with reverse-order compensation and idempotent activities.

use_cases.title: Review Workflow Reliability
use_cases.description: Assess determinism, retries, timeouts, heartbeats, and failure classification before release.

use_cases.title: Model Long-Lived Processes
use_cases.description: Choose entity workflows, signals, queries, and callbacks for approvals or account lifecycles.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Workflow Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify these process steps as Temporal workflows or activities: [steps]. Explain each boundary and identify missing inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Saga
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Temporal saga for [business process]. List forward steps, compensations, execution order, and idempotency requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Review Resilience
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this workflow design: [design]. Recommend retry policies, timeouts, non-retryable errors, heartbeats, and failure recovery checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design for Scale and Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [workflow] for replay safety, versioning, child workflow decomposition, task queues, observability, and bounded execution.

output_examples.input: Design an order workflow with inventory, payment, and fulfillment.
output_examples.output: Use a saga. Register release, refund, and cancellation compensations before each activity, then run successful compensations in reverse order after failure.

output_examples.input: Review a workflow that reads system time and calls a payment API.
output_examples.output: Replace system time with Temporal workflow time. Move the payment call into an idempotent activity with explicit timeout and retry policies.

output_examples.input: Scale one workflow that coordinates one million tasks.
output_examples.output: Partition work across bounded child workflows, aggregate results, and monitor queue depth, execution duration, retries, and failures.

best_practices: Keep workflows deterministic and place external interactions inside activities.
Register compensations before forward actions and make every activity idempotent.
Set explicit timeouts, classify errors, and heartbeat long-running activities.
anti_patterns: Do not call databases, files, networks, or nondeterministic libraries directly from workflows.
Do not retry validation failures or permanent business rule violations.
Do not place unbounded task volumes inside one workflow execution.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design Temporal workflows, activities, compensation, retries, callbacks, entity lifecycles, and scalable execution.

faq.question: Does it generate complete Temporal code?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns, review guidance, and design recommendations rather than production-ready code.

faq.question: Why must workflows be deterministic?
faq.answer: Temporal replays event history to restore state. Nondeterministic decisions can produce results that conflict with recorded events.

faq.question: When should I use an activity?
faq.answer: Use an activity for database access, network calls, file operations, email delivery, payments, and other external interactions.

faq.question: How should failed saga steps be handled?
faq.answer: Register each compensation before its forward step, then execute applicable compensations in reverse order.

faq.question: Can this skill validate my deployment settings?
faq.answer: No. Verify retry limits, payload constraints, worker capacity, task queues, and observability in your own environment.
